verdict.rationale: Modal's own docs show you attach GPUs to a Function with the `gpu` argument and deploy it as a serverless application. Its endpoints scale with traffic and idle at zero, and containers spin up and down in 1-2 seconds. That covers serverless GPU workers that autoscale and scale to zero, with no always-on instances to manage. missing for 10: in-depth autoscaler/scale-to-zero configuration docs (the claims come from the homepage and pricing pages), independent or hands-on corroboration of cold-start and scale-to-zero behavior.

support.subject: As a developer, I can deploy code to autoscaling serverless GPU workers that scale to zero, instead of managing always-on instances

citations.quote: You can pick a specific GPU type for your Function via the `gpu` argument.
The [Modal](https://modal.com/) Python SDK allows you to deploy high-performance serverless applications and programmatically interact with the Modal platform.
Turn any function into an HTTPS endpoint that scales with traffic and idles at zero.
In contrast, _Modal spins containers_ up and down in 1-2 seconds.
Fan out over thousands of GPUs, fully parallel, no job orchestration to manage.
